rationale: C23 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. Both letters answer a New Hampshire state election official's telegram about petition-driven placement of the President's name on the presidential-preference primary ballot; express gratitude to the petitioners; decline to object to or seek removal of the name; clarify that this acquiescence is not a decision to seek another term; and justify the position by emphasizing voters' freedom to choose. The child substantially expands and adapts that same sequence to Eisenhower's health-related uncertainty. C04 shares some voting-choice rhetoric but not the specific situation or structure, while C11 links illness to delayed decision-making but otherwise concerns an unrelated diplomatic matter.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have your courteous telegram ... advising me that petitions have been filed at your office which qualify my name for inclusion on the Presidential preference primary ballot ... Naturally, I am deeply gratified that the petitioners have expressed this kind of personal confidence in me.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Thank you very much for your telegram concerning the Presidential Preference Primary in New Hampshire. I am most grateful to those who signed the petitions in my behalf.
shared_material.explanation: Both open by acknowledging a telegram from a New Hampshire election official and thanking the people whose petitions placed the President on the primary ballot.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I do not feel that I should interpose any objection to such entry. However ... lack of objection cannot be construed as any final decision on my part relative to a candidacy for a second term
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I shall not ask you to take my name off the list ... until I am ready to make an announcement as to whether I shall seek reelection.
shared_material.explanation: Both decline to remove or object to the name while expressly separating ballot inclusion from the unresolved decision whether to seek another term.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Freedom to select, nominate and elect a candidate to public office is basic to our American political system ... every citizen should have the widest possible choice in expressing his own preference
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have long favored a nationwide Presidential primary, so that the voters could really choose their own candidates.
shared_material.explanation: Both ground the decision in voter choice, with the child elaborating the same rationale.
